To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

T cells establish specific immunological synapses with target cells in vivo and in allogeneic cultures, and that these synapses induce a dramatic reorganization of the target cells' cytoskeleton, resulting in the target cells becoming polarized towards the immunological contacts with the effector T cell.
immunological synapses formed by effector T cell induce a novel polarization of target astroglial cells, both in vivo and in vivo.
astrocytes respond differently to immune T cells depending on the nature of the T cell response.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of T cells in the brain.
understanding the mechanisms of how T cells induce polarization of astrocytes, and the consequences of this polarization on the immune response to viral infection, and to other diseases of the brain.
how astrocytes respond when attacked by effector T lymphocytes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

T cells can induce astrocyte polarization in vitro and in situ, as well as T cells being able to induce astrocyte hypertrophic response in vivo and in situ, and that these two mechanisms of astrocyte response are independent and not interrelated.
the immunological synapses formed between T cells and astrocytes are capable of polarizing the astrocytes, and that the MTOC and Golgi stacks become polarized in response to the synapses.
the polarization of target astroctyes in response to immunolgical synapses is an important mechanism of astrocyte response to cellular injury.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

astrocytes, in addition to hypertrophy, can respond to T cell attack by undergoing a major structural reorganizational change, becoming polarized towards the immunological synaptic contact with the effector T cell.
T cells induce polarization of target cells in vivo and in vivo.
immunological synapses can induce astrocyte polarization, which may be a novel response mechanism to cellular injury.

the formation of immunosynapses by T cells is able to induce a dramatic morphological change of astrocytes, which may be important in regulating astrocyte responses to T cells in the CNS.
